sources.entry: wxPython - A cross-platform GUI toolkit that wraps the wxWidgets C++ library.

summary.one_liner: wxPython Project Phoenix is the next-generation wxPython, a Python binding that wraps the wxWidgets C++ GUI toolkit, and this repo holds its source and build system.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a developer guide for building wxPython from a Git checkout rather than a user guide for using the library. It describes the build_wxpy.py command-line tool, with commands for generating code (dox, etg, sip), building wxWidgets and Phoenix (build), running tests, and cleaning up. It explains that wxWidgets is pulled in as a git submodule at ext/wxWidgets, and that an already-installed wxWidgets can be used with --use_syswx. It also describes the project layout (etg, etgtools, sip, wx, buildtools folders) and the per-platform prerequisites for Windows, Linux and macOS. Release binaries are said to be available on PyPI, and snapshot builds are linked from the README.
use_cases: create native desktop GUI in Python
how_to_run: python build_wxpy.py dox etg --nodoc sip build
notable: Wraps the wxWidgets C++ toolkit to give Python apps native-looking GUIs on Windows, macOS and Unix
Code bindings are generated by an Extractor-Tweaker-Generator (etg) pipeline from wxWidgets Doxygen XML
Build tool can bundle relocatable wxWidgets shared libraries inside the wx package
Successor to 'Classic' wxPython, aiming at better speed and maintainability
caveats: Building from source is complex; the README says binaries on PyPI suit most users
Windows builds need Visual Studio 2015 and may need Cygwin; Mingw32 is not supported without script changes
Linux builds need many -dev packages (GTK3, WebKit2GTK, etc.)
Using an external wxWidgets requires a version close in age to the Phoenix code
keywords: make a desktop app with python
